Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood as replacement for current LLM provider (OpenAI). Primary path: start on Hosted API for fast parity testing, then move to Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and cost. Team: CTO (J. Alvarez), Head of AI (K. Morgan), Platform Eng (S. Li). AE: Maya Chen; SE: Ravi Patel; CSM assigned post-close: Elena Torres.

Recent context / ask: they want end-to-end migration playbook: 1) compatibility layer (headers + rate-limit translation) 2) prompt parity test suite and regression detection 3) model routing policy for fallback to cheaper variant during spikes. High sensitivity to latency for support workflows (p90 < 400ms for short prompts) and embeddings rerank throughput (target ~120 qps at peak). Cost target: reduce per-conversation token cost by 20% vs current spend.

POC details: started hosted-api POC 2026-01-08. Ran sample traffic replay (200k tokens/day) over 2 weeks. Observed 3 prompt regressions (formatting + system message handling) affecting summarization outputs. SE created prompt-adjustment plan and added a small adapter layer to preserve system-role semantics (notes in Drive). Next step is Dedicated sizing run for sustained 8k tokens/sec during business hours.

Artifacts / refs: POC transcript ff-8231, drive deck with pricing scenarios (linked), early prompt parity spreadsheet (gthread-9876543210 thread includes sample diffs). Raised INF-3421 to investigate a batching-induced latency spike during replay.

Commercials: mid-sized ARR profile, willing to commit to 12 month Reserved Dedicated if POC meets parity and latency SLOs. Initial pricing conversation: estimated ARR 75k-150k depending on ingress/outbound data retention terms.

Decision factors: technical parity, SLA-backed latency guarantees, predictable unit economics (batching/quantization suggestions), ease of routing from hosted→dedicated, and an ops playbook for regressions.
